entries.test: Meta's published fake-account prevalence estimates and independent studies of how common AI-generated content is on Facebook in early 2025.
entries.note: The proposition leaves out the hyperbolic 'nonsense groups' clause but keeps the testable core. 'Crammed' is vague, but there is a shared reading: these things are widespread.
Whether coverage 'turned its back on the truth' or 'pumped up' AI is an editorial judgment that readers would assess differently.

entries.test: OpenAI's reported 2024 net loss or cash burn, widely reported at roughly $5 billion.
entries.note: He states this as a fact inside a sentence about Newton.
Whether a 'path to profitability' exists right now is contested and has no shared test. Only actual profitability, which is a separate forecast, could settle it.

entries.test: Reporting on when Meta's AI persona accounts launched (around September 2023) and whether Meta deleted them after the FT story in January 2025.
entries.note: 'So unpopular nobody noticed' is loose, but the timeline and the deletion can be checked.

entries.test: Whether Meta has brought back its own AI-run profile or character accounts on Facebook or Instagram.
entries.note: This is a firm forecast ('100% sure') with no deadline. The 'intends' clause is a stated motive and cannot be checked itself.

entries.test: Independent measurements of the share of AI-generated content among posts recommended or seen on Facebook in early 2025.
entries.note: 'Dominates' is vague, but the plain reading is that AI content is the prevailing share of what users see.
He offers his belief about what Zuckerberg is attempting, and the quoted lines are his own paraphrases, not real quotes. The proposition drops 'I believe' and 'attempting' and states it as fact.
A 'Slop Era' in which experiences 'rot' has no shared measure for readers to test.

entries.test: Whether Meta substantially expanded AI-generated content in Facebook and Instagram feeds, for example dedicated AI-content feeds or AI posts it promotes.
entries.note: 'As much as it wants' is hyperbole. The plain reading is a large increase in the AI content Meta pushes.

entries.test: Google's January 2025 increase to Workspace prices with Gemini bundled in (about $2 per user per month), and Microsoft's January 2025 increase to consumer Microsoft 365 prices with Copilot bundled in.
entries.note: The proposition drops the specifics: the $2 Workspace increase and the fact that Microsoft's rise was for consumer Office. 'Customers don't want' is the softer part of the claim.
He calls it his 'hypothesis', a tentative framing, which the drafter rendered as 'probably'.
Calling the companies 'desperate' is a claim about their motive, which public evidence cannot settle.
